input: Check the crawl space for moisture damage

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a quick visual scan or a thorough inspection (insulation, wood, pipes, vapor barrier, mold) determines how detailed the checklist needs to be.
Whether the user is doing this themselves or hiring a professional changes the entire plan — tools needed, safety steps, and what to look for.
The crawl space's current condition (never inspected vs. recently checked) and any known history of water issues affects what to prioritize.
Physical limitations of the crawl space (height, access point, lighting) and any time or budget constraints affect how and when this can be done.
Knowing what tools and protective gear the user already has on hand determines whether they need to gather supplies before starting.
Whether the goal is just documentation, a pass/fail assessment, or producing a repair plan changes what 'done' looks like.
Whether the user wants to fix issues themselves or hand findings off to a contractor shapes how the output of the inspection should be recorded.

gold.taskTitle: Inspect crawl space for moisture damage
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to inspect their crawl space to identify any signs of moisture damage and determine what, if anything, needs to be addressed.

questions.title: Which areas of the crawl space are you inspecting?
questions.description: Is this a full inspection covering all sections — wood framing, insulation, vapor barrier, pipes, vents — or focused on a specific area of concern?

questions.title: Are you doing this yourself or hiring a professional?
questions.description: A DIY inspection requires a personal safety and tools checklist, while hiring a pro shifts the task toward finding and briefing a contractor.

questions.title: Has this crawl space had any known water or moisture issues before?
questions.description: Prior flooding, standing water, or past repairs are critical context that determines which warning signs to prioritize during the inspection.

questions.title: How accessible and large is the crawl space?
questions.description: The height clearance, entry point size, and total area affect the time required, safety precautions needed, and whether special equipment is necessary.

questions.title: What tools and protective gear do you currently have?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user has a flashlight, moisture meter, respirator, coveralls, and knee pads determines whether a supply-gathering step is needed first.

questions.title: What does a successful inspection look like to you?
questions.description: Is the goal a simple yes/no on whether damage exists, a written report with photos, or a prioritized list of repairs to action?

questions.title: Do you plan to fix any issues found yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: A DIY repair plan requires sourcing materials and methods, while a contractor handoff means the output should be a clear damage summary to share.
